query: Which material can be used for ductility, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Copper exhibits enhanced ductility when subjected to annealing processes.
generation.conditions: Heating copper to a specific temperature followed by controlled cooling
generation.mechanism: Recrystallization of the cold-worked microstructure leading to reduced dislocation density
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased ductility of copper after annealing
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is limited to copper and does not apply to other materials or different heat treatment processes.
generation.uncertainty: The specific temperature and duration of the annealing process may vary and affect the outcome.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct a series of tensile tests on cold-worked copper samples before and after annealing at various temperatures.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the ductility of the annealed samples does not exceed that of the cold-worked samples, the hypothesis is falsified.
